issues.description: Silent semantic change: coerceNumber maps null/NaN to 0 instead of propagating NaN as the old toNumber did.
issues.detail: Original lift used toNumber, which returned null for non-numeric input and produced NaN downstream (visibly wrong). New coerceNumber silently substitutes 0, distorting domains on malformed input. This is a real runtime behavior change hidden inside a 'just added types' PR. Either preserve NaN propagation or document the new contract in the commit message.

issues.description: Domain typed as number[] with runtime guard, instead of NonEmptyArray<number> at the boundary.
issues.detail: Public signatures still accept number[] then runtime-check via isNonEmpty, defeating the point of typing. A NonEmptyArray<number> (or readonly [number, number, ...number[]]) signature pushes the constraint to compile time and makes the runtime throw a real backstop. The actual invariant is |domain| >= 2, since code reads both domain[0] and peek(domain) as distinct endpoints.

issues.description: Local identity reintroduced as a one-liner instead of reusing the shared accessors.identity.
issues.detail: Original imported identity from ./accessors.js. New file inlines a typed identity: TransformFn = x => x and drops the import. Functionally equivalent for numbers but duplicates an existing utility and diverges from codebase voice. Either fix the shared identity's type once or justify the narrower local in a comment.

issues.description: peek overload pair is more machinery than needed and doesn't fire at internal call sites.
issues.detail: The non-empty overload only narrows when callers pass a tuple type, which pan/zoom don't after isNonEmpty. So peek still returns number | undefined internally and arithmetic silently coerces to NaN. If domains were typed as NonEmptyArray at the boundary, the overload would be unnecessary. At minimum, add a comment explaining intended use.

issues.description: Empty-domain test coverage is Linear-only; Log/Pow/Symlog paths are untested and read domain[0] pre-guard.
issues.detail: panLog/zoomLog call Math.sign(domain[0]) before delegating to pan/zoom, so empty domains briefly produce sign=NaN before the throw fires. The error still triggers, but the order is sloppy and only Linear is tested. A small table-driven test across all eight entry points would prove the contract cheaply.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees: this is a small, readable TypeScript port of transform.js with one quiet semantic change that must be owned — coerceNumber silently maps null/NaN to 0, where the old toNumber-based lift propagated NaN visibly. The typing is half-done: public signatures still accept number[] and rely on a runtime isNonEmpty throw, when a NonEmptyArray<number> at the boundary would eliminate the guard, simplify peek, and make the contract real. Tests cover only Linear empty-domain behavior; Log/Pow/Symlog variants poke domain[0] before the throw and are untested. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK — fix coerceNumber semantics (or document them), tighten the Domain type at the public edge, and broaden the empty-domain tests.
